description: The MPEG-TS PMT parser in libavformat/mpegts.c allocates a fixed 16-entry (1152-byte) Mp4Descr array on the stack and, for each IOD_DESCRIPTOR in the program_info loop, calls mp4_read_iods() with a base pointer offset by the accumulated count but a constant limit of MAX_MP4_DESCR_COUNT (16). mp4_read_iods()/init_MP4DescrParseContext() reset the local descr_count to 0, so the bounds check in parse_MP4ESDescrTag compares 0 against 16 and always passes. A PMT containing two IOD descriptors of 16 ESDescrs each fills slots 0..15 on the first pass and then writes slots 16..31 on the second, overflowing the stack array by 1152 bytes. The bug fires inside avformat_open_input(), so simply running ffprobe on a crafted file is enough to trigger it.
location: parse_MP4ESDescrTag() at libavformat/mpegts.c:1570; called from pmt_cb() at mpegts.c:2616
reproduction: 1. Craft an MPEG-TS stream with a PMT whose program_info loop contains two IOD_DESCRIPTOR entries.
2. Populate each IOD with 16 ESDescr entries (MAX_MP4_DESCR_COUNT).
3. Deliver the file to the target (e.g. upload to a transcoding service, or get a user to run ffprobe/ffmpeg on it).

4. avformat_open_input() parses the PMT; the first IOD fills mp4_descr[0..15]; the second IOD receives base = mp4_descr+16 with a fresh limit of 16 and writes mp4_descr[16..31], 1152 bytes past the stack array.
technical_details:
Hi --

I've got another vulnerability with Claude. This one is in the MPEG-TS

PMT parser and dates to fec2836483 (from October 2011).

It fires inside avformat_open_input, so again ffprobe alone triggers it:

  ffprobe attack.mp4

The bug is in pmt_cb(), in libavformat/mpegts.c. The PMT program_info

loop walks the list of descriptors, and for each IOD_DESCRIPTOR it

calls mp4_read_iods():

  // mpegts.c

  int mp4_descr_count = 0;

  Mp4Descr mp4_descr[MAX_MP4_DESCR_COUNT] = { { 0 } };  // 16 * 72 = 1152B stack

  ...

  if (tag == IOD_DESCRIPTOR && len >= 2) {

      ...

      mp4_read_iods(ts->stream, p, len,

                    mp4_descr + mp4_descr_count,    // base shifts forward

                    &mp4_descr_count,

                    MAX_MP4_DESCR_COUNT);           // but limit stays at 16

  }

In the code above, the base pointer advances by the running count, but

the capacity argument is always 16. Inside, mp4_read_iods() resets its

own counter to 0 and the bounds check compares that against 16:

  // init_MP4DescrParseContext

  d->descr_count = 0;

  // parse_MP4ESDescrTag

  if (d->descr_count >= d->max_descr_count)   // 0 >= 16?

      return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;

  d->active_descr = d->descr + (d->descr_count++);

  d->active_descr->es_id = es_id;             // OOB write

The PoC creates a PMT with two IOD descriptors of 16 ESDescrs each.

The first fills mp4_descr[0..15], and the second gets base = mp4_descr

+ 16 with a fresh count of 0 and writes mp4_descr[16..31]. Every write

in the second IOD is past the end of the stack array, for 1152 bytes

total.

I've tested against the current master and hit an ASAN again:

  ==1999653==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow

  WRITE of size 4 at 0x73054bb01b60 thread T0

      #0 parse_MP4ESDescrTag libavformat/mpegts.c:1570:28

      ...

      #6 pmt_cb libavformat/mpegts.c:2616

      #7 write_section_data libavformat/mpegts.c:474

      ...

      #11 avformat_open_input libavformat/demux.c:323

    [1760, 2912) 'mp4_descr' (line 2548) <== access at offset 2912 overflows

I'm unsure again exactly how you would prefer a fix. It looks like

multiple IODs are required by the spec (if I'm reading ISO/IEC

13818-1:2007 sec 2.6.40 right), so I'm not really sure the best way to

handle this.

One way would be to increment the count (instead of just assign) and

then offset in the calls to read. I'm not sure if this is a fix that

you'd like, but it does prevent the PoC.

diff --git a/libavformat/mpegts.c b/libavformat/mpegts.c

index bfbdbf5b19..4b326d309b 100644

--- a/libavformat/mpegts.c

+++ b/libavformat/mpegts.c

@@ -1703,7 +1703,7 @@ static int mp4_read_iods(AVFormatContext *s,

const uint8_t *buf, unsigned size,

     ret = parse_mp4_descr(&d, avio_tell(&d.pb.pub), size, MP4IODescrTag);

-    *descr_count = d.descr_count;

+    *descr_count += d.descr_count;

     return ret;

 }

@@ -2614,7 +2614,7 @@ static void pmt_cb(MpegTSFilter *filter, const

uint8_t *section, int section_len

             get8(&p, p_end); // label

             len -= 2;

             mp4_read_iods(ts->stream, p, len, mp4_descr + mp4_descr_count,

-                          &mp4_descr_count, MAX_MP4_DESCR_COUNT);

+                          &mp4_descr_count, MAX_MP4_DESCR_COUNT -

mp4_descr_count);

         } else if (tag == REGISTRATION_DESCRIPTOR && len >= 4) {

             prog_reg_desc = bytestream_get_le32(&p);

             len -= 4;

Thanks,

Nicholas
title: Stack buffer overflow in mpegts.c pmt_cb via multiple IOD
